what_happened: While job 20261016-044847-hem1 was being verified, the verifier failed with "No space left on device". An operator deleted the cargo target/ build caches of two idle, finished job workspaces (2fsa at 9.9G and g61b at 5.2G). That freed 15G. Finished job workspaces had kept their build caches indefinitely, and those caches filled the disk.
cause: Nothing in Athena owns disk lifecycle. Workspaces of finished jobs are never cleaned, so large regenerable build artifacts pile up without limit. No pre-flight check of free space runs before a job or its verification starts, and no alert warns when space is low. The disk limit therefore shows up only as a failure inside the verifier, and an operator has to find and clear the space by hand.
prevention: Two code-enforced steps. (1) When a job reaches a terminal state (merged, closed or rejected and not retryable), delete its regenerable build directories such as cargo target/. A periodic sweep should also remove these directories from idle workspaces older than a set age. (2) Before the verifier or any job starts, check free space against a minimum threshold, for example 10G. If space is below the threshold, run the cleanup sweep first. If it is still below, pause the job with a clear "environment: low disk" status instead of running it and failing. A low-disk status must not count as a rejection of the work.
proposed_request: Stop finished job workspaces from filling the disk. When a job reaches a terminal state, Athena should automatically delete its regenerable build caches (such as cargo target/ directories). A periodic sweep should also clear those caches from idle workspaces. Before starting any job or verification, Athena should check that free disk space is above a configured minimum. If space is low, it should run the cleanup first. If space is still low, it should hold the job with an explicit "low disk" status and notify the operator. It must not run the verifier and reject the work as unproven. Show that the behavior works: with a simulated low-disk condition, the cleanup runs, the job is held rather than rejected, and verification proceeds once space is freed.
